claims.text: The official LeetCode 143 statement requires reordering L0→L1→…→Ln into L0→Ln→L1→Ln-1→… without modifying node values, and gives [1,2,3,4]→[1,4,2,3] and [1,2,3,4,5]→[1,5,2,4,3] as examples.

The candidate's split-at-front-half-tail, reverse-second-half, then alternating-merge implementation produces the required node order for odd and even lengths while preserving node identities and values and introducing no cycle in the reproducible validation set.

The implementation performs one linear midpoint scan, one linear reversal of the second half, and one linear merge while using only a constant number of pointer variables, supporting O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims. The validation covers lengths 1..64, official examples, duplicate-value identity checks, node-count preservation, value preservation, and acyclicity.

checks: generated lengths 1..64 against independent array-order oracle

findings: The candidate matches the official LeetCode 143 problem contract and examples and does not mutate node values.
The three-stage explanation is mechanically complete: midpoint split, explicit disconnect, in-place second-half reversal, and alternating merge with saved successors.
The implementation handles odd and even list lengths correctly; the middle node remains naturally in place for odd lengths when the second half is exhausted.
The stated O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary-space bounds are consistent with the implementation.
The reproducible validation is stronger than example-only checking because it verifies order, acyclicity, node count, node identity, and value preservation.
The project-experience section explicitly avoids fabricating production or interview experience.
